claims.text: Conventional metal parts in hot-dip aluminum plating equipment are prone to rapid corrosion during direct contact with molten aluminum.
A dense Al2O3-based ceramic coating can protect metal parts from molten-aluminum corrosion.
A dense spinel coating can protect metal parts from molten-aluminum corrosion.
Thermal spraying or pack cementation can be used to apply the proposed protective ceramic layer.
Hot-dip aluminum plating exposes equipment to molten aluminum at approximately 660°C.
The applied coating will form an inert, continuous ceramic barrier on the metal substrate.
The continuous ceramic barrier prevents direct contact and reaction between molten aluminum and the underlying metal.
The ceramic coating is chemically inert and thermally stable under the stated molten-aluminum exposure conditions.
Preventing reaction between molten aluminum and the substrate preserves the equipment's structural integrity.
Coated parts will have significantly lower corrosion rates than uncoated parts under identical high-temperature conditions.
Coated parts will have a longer service life than uncoated parts under identical high-temperature conditions.
Non-uniformity or mechanical damage can limit the coating's protective effectiveness.
Thermal cycling beyond the coating's stability range can limit its protective effectiveness.
Protection established near 660°C may not persist at significantly higher temperatures without modification.
